reader.requirement: At 1985 (Amendment 1 as amended by X3.23b-1993, C314), when FUNCTION MAX has more than one argument-1 all must be of the same class (numeric, alphanumeric, alphabetic, where numeric-edited, alphanumeric-edited and group items are class alphanumeric), except that alphabetic and alphanumeric arguments may be mixed; the compiler must refuse a list that mixes numeric with alphabetic/alphanumeric, and accept every same-class or alphabetic/alphanumeric list, including ALL-subscripted tables, expressions and nested functions.

reader.notes: CrossViolation intersects each argument's TableTwoClass projection after CrossBlock merges alphabetic into alphanumeric, which is exactly the amended 1985 rule; numeric-edited and group items project to alphanumeric as 1985 classes them. The diagnostic text cites §2023:15.59.3 r2 rather than the 1985 clause even at --std 85 (wording only, the refusal is correct).

refuter.evidence: §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR3a: 'If an ALL subscript is specified for an operand, the reference-modifier is applied to each of the implicitly specified elements of the table'; GR5: a ref-modified numeric item is 'considered class and category alphanumeric'. So N-EL (ALL) (2:1) over a PIC 9(2) table is a list of class alphanumeric arguments. Probe src/allrmmix.cob at --std 85 (runs/allrmmix-001): FUNCTION MAX (N-EL (ALL) (2:1) "1") is REFUSED with COBOL1627 'argument-2 is of class alphanumeric, which cannot agree with the earlier arguments' although every argument is class alphanumeric (rejects legal source). Probe src/allrmmax.cob (runs/allrmmax-001): DISPLAY FUNCTION MAX (N-EL (ALL) (1:1) N-ITEM) mixes class alphanumeric with class numeric and compiles with NO diagnostic at --std 85 (under-rejects); at --std 2023 (runs/allrmmax-002) it compiles and crashes at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException 'FUNCTION MAX in a string context'. Control: the non-ALL form is right (src/rmmaxok.cob runs/rmmaxok-002: MAX (N-ITEM (1:2) X-ITEM) -> 5A, MAX (A-ITEM N-ITEM (3:2)) -> QZ). Cause: IntrinsicBinder.TryBindTableAll wraps the RefModPlace view in a TableAllPlace, and IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOfPlace only recognises a bare RefModPlace, so it falls to ClassOfItem(p.Item) = the numeric element. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR3a  (4.3.8.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3a'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5  (4.3.8.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5'; 'OK  §1989:A.2.23.3 AR1  (2.23.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR1'; 'OK  §1989:A.2.2  (2.2 ARGUMENTS**)  the text is in the clause; it lies in AR4' (the ALL 'as if each table element ... were specified' sentence).
refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING (rejects-legal-source and under-rejects), cause (c): the rule's argument classes at 1985 include an ALL-subscripted reference-modified numeric table, which is class alphanumeric by §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR3a/GR5; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#ClassOfPlace classes a TableAllPlace over a RefModPlace by its element item (numeric). Same at --std 2023 (refusal identical; the under-rejected mix crashes at run time).

adjudication.reason: A reference-modified element under an ALL subscript (`N-EL (ALL) (1:1)`) is class alphanumeric by the 1985 text, and the argument-class screen classes it as its numeric element. MAX and MIN refuse legal lists; MEAN, MEDIAN and MIDRANGE compute from digit slices; an illegal MAX mix compiles and fails at run time. Not the mechanism of PB5780 or PB5813.
